name: Donepezil
route_note: Once-daily oral tablet or orally disintegrating tablet; weekly transdermal patch in the US.

discovery.note: A piperidine-based acetylcholinesterase inhibitor discovered by Eisai after a screening programme begun in 1983.

tagline: The most widely used cholinesterase inhibitor for Alzheimer's disease
summary: Donepezil is a once-daily acetylcholinesterase inhibitor that modestly improves cognition and function in Alzheimer's disease. Discovered by Eisai and co-marketed with Pfizer as Aricept, it became the best-selling dementia drug before generics arrived.
mechanism: Alzheimer's disease involves early loss of basal forebrain cholinergic neurons. Donepezil reversibly and selectively inhibits acetylcholinesterase, the enzyme that hydrolyses acetylcholine at synapses, increasing cholinergic transmission in remaining circuits.
Its effect is symptomatic: it does not alter amyloid or tau pathology, and benefits on cognitive scales are modest and vary between individuals.
uses: Mild, moderate and severe dementia of the Alzheimer's type

history.title: Research begins
history.detail: Eisai starts the programme that leads to E2020 (donepezil).

history.title: US approval
history.detail: The FDA approves Aricept for mild-to-moderate Alzheimer's disease, marketed by Eisai and Pfizer.

history.title: Japan approval
history.detail: Donepezil becomes the first Alzheimer's drug approved in Japan.

history.title: Severe disease
history.detail: The FDA extends approval to severe Alzheimer's disease.

history.title: 23 mg tablet and generics
history.detail: A higher-dose 23 mg tablet is approved and US generics of the standard strengths launch.

history.title: Namzaric
history.detail: A fixed-dose combination of memantine extended-release and donepezil is approved in the US.

history.title: Transdermal patch
history.detail: The FDA approves a weekly donepezil patch (Adlarity).

facts: Donepezil's discoverer Hachiro Sugimoto has said the research was motivated in part by his mother's dementia.
